preamble: Anniversary puzzle for a time of change

clue.text: Name of female officer in charge at cathedral

parts.note: C-in-C, commander-in-chief, is the officer in overall charge of the forces
Ely is the cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A woman is the officer running things at a cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a girl's given name, an old English form of Cecilia.

clue.text: Church member arrested according to report

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word for arrested is spoken

parts.note: copped is slang for arrested, nabbed

explanation.surface: A churchgoer is said to have been nicked by the police.
explanation.definitionFit: A Copt belongs to the Coptic Christian Church of Egypt.

clue.text: Sri Lanka affair producing outcry

parts.note: CL is the international vehicle registration code for Sri Lanka
an amour is a love affair

explanation.surface: A scandal in Sri Lanka causes public uproar.
explanation.definitionFit: Clamour is a loud protest or outcry.

clue.text: Large? Then it's bad place for one to enter!

definitions.text: Large? Then it's bad place for one to enter!

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: the word for one goes into the run of bad and place

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill will
put means to place
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: If you are big, this is not a good place to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to enter' puts the numeral inside the run of bad plus place. The whole clue describes Swift's island of tiny people in Gulliver's Travels, no place for a big person.
explanation.definitionFit: Swift's land of six-inch people is a hopeless destination for any large visitor.

clue.text: Mates — the type to engage in fiddles

indicators.note: the type word is taken into, engaged within, the word for fiddles

parts.note: cons are swindles or fiddles
a sort is a type or kind

explanation.surface: Mates are the sort of people who get involved in petty swindles.
explanation.definitionFit: Consorts are partners or spouses, so mates in the marital sense.

clue.text: After men box, get judge to score

indicators.note: puts the word for box after the word for men

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers, men
a chest is a box
to rate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: Once the fighters have boxed, a referee is brought in to tally the points.
explanation.definitionFit: To orchestrate is to arrange music for an orchestra, i.e. to score it.

clue.text: Woman, see, wanting head removed!

parts.note: Sal is a short form of Sally or Sarah

indicators.note: the first letter of the see word is cut off

parts.note: Rome is the Holy See, the Pope's diocese

explanation.surface: Look: a woman who wants someone decapitated.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue describes Herod's step-daughter, who asked for John the Baptist's head on a platter; 'wanting' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical dancer demanded the Baptist's head as her reward from Herod.

clue.text: Rest, half of that being lost with bad feeling

indicators.note: only the front half of that word is kept for the answer
says the other half of the word goes missing

parts.note: refers back to the clue's first word, rest
spite is malice, bad feeling

explanation.surface: A break where half the time is wasted, along with some ill will.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of that being lost' keeps RE from REST, since 'that' points back to the clue's first word.
explanation.definitionFit: A respite is a short break or period of rest.

clue.text: Call to have a leftie imprisoned not restricted to one person

indicators.note: the left-winger is locked up inside the call

parts.note: to shout is to call out
a Red is a communist, a leftie

explanation.surface: Someone demands that a left-winger be jailed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something parcelled among several people is distributed, not kept by one individual.

clue.text: Like a certain king or queen somewhere in London, you'd say

definitions.text: Like a certain king or queen

indicators.note: spoken out, the place name sounds like the word wanted

parts.note: Purley is a district in the London borough of Croydon

explanation.surface: A Cockney king or queen is described as coming from some London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Pearly kings and queens are London costermonger figures in suits covered with pearl buttons; Purley is a south London suburb.
explanation.definitionFit: A costermonger king or queen in button-covered dress is known by this adjective, so it describes such royalty.

clue.text: Goon the reverse of excellent for the Church

parts.note: Eccles was a character in the radio comedy The Goon Show

indicators.note: tells us to turn the term for excellent round

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, excellent, written here as AI

explanation.surface: A comic character is anything but excellent as far as the Church is concerned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the reverse of' turns A1 round. The Goon Show was a 1950s BBC radio comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecclesia is the Greek-derived word for an assembly of believers, i.e. a church.

clue.text: Last words of 21? Others weep with him, I fancy

indicators.note: as an adjective, fancy suggests elaborate rearrangement of the preceding words

explanation.surface: Asked about a king's dying words, the speaker imagines others weeping with him.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of OTHERS WEEP HIM I gives the phrase; 'with' is only a link. The words are those reputedly spoken by the king at 21 on his deathbed in 1936.
explanation.definitionFit: Reputedly the dying monarch asked how his realm was faring, so this question is his famous final utterance.

clue.text: Occasions when many top performers get dismissed? Try strike action maybe

definitions.text: Occasions when many top performers get dismissed?

parts.note: to test is to try
matches are things you strike to make a flame

explanation.surface: Industrial action might be tried when stars are sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike action' wants to be industrial action, but it is the striking of matches. Test matches are full international cricket games, where top batsmen are dismissed (got out).
explanation.definitionFit: International cricket fixtures are where the best batsmen are got out, a cricketing sense of dismissed.

clue.text: Fringe benefit for each is brought in fairly

parts.note: per means for each, as in per head

indicators.note: the word is goes inside the word for fairly

parts.note: quite means fairly, moderately

explanation.surface: Each employee is given a fair perk.
explanation.definitionFit: A perquisite, often shortened to perk, is a benefit received on top of salary.

clue.text: Chunk of words — the normal amount to accompany a diagram

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
a graph is a diagram

explanation.surface: A typical length of text sits beside a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragraph is a distinct section of writing, a block of text.

clue.text: American city that has French artist but no Irish

indicators.note: says the abbreviation for Irish is to be dropped from the painter's name

parts.note: Pierre-Auguste Renoir was the French Impressionist painter

explanation.surface: A US city boasts a French painter but no Irish ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Reno is a gambling city in Nevada, in the United States.

clue.text: Fairy's the female mischief-maker

parts.note: a peri is a fairy in Persian myth, here with its 's
her is the female pronoun

explanation.surface: A fairy is said to be the troublemaking woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Perisher is British slang for an annoying or mischievous person, often a child.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a pesky, troublesome person, especially a naughty child.

clue.text: Newspaper editor's prime passion

parts.note: rag is slang for a low-quality newspaper

indicators.note: the prime part of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An editor's main enthusiasm is the paper itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Rage is fury or intense passion, also a craze.

clue.text: Drink and drive? Stuff that!

parts.note: grog is rum and water, or drink generally
to ram is to drive in by force

explanation.surface: An angry dismissal of drinking and driving.
explanation.definitionFit: Grogram is a coarse silk fabric, and stuff is an old word for woven cloth.

clue.text: It's put into effect with penetrating article

definitions.text: It's put into effect with penetrating article

indicators.note: the article goes into the other word, penetrating it

parts.note: to implement is to carry out or put into effect
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Something is carried out using a sharp, piercing object.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue describes running something through with a stake, which is just what the word means.
explanation.definitionFit: Spearing something on a sharp stake is carrying out an act with a piercing implement.

clue.text: A degree of disorder that makes part of infirmary poor

parts.note: ENT, ear nose and throat, is a hospital department
ropy is British slang for poor quality

explanation.surface: Something is making one hospital department substandard.
explanation.definitionFit: Entropy is the measure of disorder in a physical system.

clue.text: Like language coming from drunk arguing, not good

indicators.note: a drunk jumble of the remaining letters
removes the letter for good from the word arguing

explanation.surface: Drunken bickering is unpleasant in its language.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing G from ARGUING leaves ARUIN, which is then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugrian describes the Finno-Ugric family of tongues, including Hungarian, so it means of a language group.

clue.text: See May's man get off high tree with difficulty

indicators.note: the letters are got into order only with difficulty, a rearrangement signal

explanation.surface: Someone is told to watch a man struggling to climb down from a tall tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is an invitation and a link. Queen Mary, consort of this king, was known as May before her marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Princess May of Teck married the British king who reigned 1910 to 1936, so he was her husband.

clue.text: Adam, blessed originally with garden, falling short

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of blessed
the garden word stops short of its last letter

parts.note: Eden is the biblical garden

explanation.surface: Adam was blessed at first with a garden but fell short.
explanation.walkthrough: Adam wants to be the first man in Eden; he is George Eliot's title hero.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot's 1859 novel's carpenter hero has Adam as his first name, so the surname completes him.

clue.text: Jars may be drunk after broadcast

indicators.note: places the word for drunk after the word for broadcast

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
tight is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: Jars of beer may be downed after a show goes out.
explanation.definitionFit: Sealed jars let no air in or out, so are hermetically sealed.

clue.text: Seat chucked in the auditorium

indicators.note: an auditorium is where things are heard, so the word for chucked is taken as spoken

parts.note: thrown means chucked or tossed

explanation.surface: Someone's seat is hurled across a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A throne is a ceremonial chair, the seat of a monarch.

clue.text: Fellow is locked in shed? He's unlikely to pray

indicators.note: the man and is are shut inside the shed

parts.note: a hut is a shed
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: A man locked in a shed is unlikely to be saying prayers.
explanation.definitionFit: A humanist follows a non-religious ethical outlook, so would not be praying.

clue.text: What sounds like region down below barrier

indicators.note: says the word for the body region is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: the groin is the body area at the top of the legs

explanation.surface: A coy reference to a nether body region turns into a barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A groyne is a low wall built out into the sea to check erosion, a type of barrier.
